actions.description: Class 1 independent hostile plan review before execution. Reviewer Codex CLI, gpt-6.1-sol, max; different family from Claude implementer, as recorded by the launch request. Loaded the complete operator profile (one Markdown file). Rehashed all 33 input pins: zero drift in hashes or lengths. Branch develop, HEAD e863efdf523449114535ff9ca76f0da295b9a5a3. Live native status: 163 entries, 8 modified tracked paths and 155 untracked paths; diff 222 insertions and 8 deletions, gitlink cc67418cba58e71d8e70fd353e9de47199ad2075. Supported bootstrap and beginTurn succeeded with persisted=true. Historical failsafe depth 2 observed only; no queue replay, hook repair, settings change, cancellation or native build. Parent linkage is in beginTurn tags. All review scripts and evidence remain in the round 3b directory. The requested openSession generated a child-local state, while beginTurn used the plugin bootstrap session; identity is corrected to the actual persisted receipt rather than the unused proposed id.

Independent source rechecks: the 20 historical patch hunks map to H1-H12, including the previously omitted mainviccpu bootstrap at patch line 230; raw consumer scans independently reproduce 56 semantic-token candidate files and 43 original-token files (5 with Category), not a semantic per-method inventory. Fixture byte parsing reaches exact EOF and reproduces MAINCPU 1.2 clk 109163946, PC 22377, DRIVE8 payload has_tde=0/has_drives=1. Fourteen inspected materialization files match the pinned Git blobs. Live supported effective-requirements read found all five requested records pending; FR-VICE mapping links TR-VICE-ORACLE-001 and TEST-VICE-001; TODO tasks 4 and 5 open. New substantive gaps under review: the original VSF plan requires xvic PAL and NTSC fixtures at 100000 cycles while revision 3 specifies reset dumps; full selected Test also contains the managed-only Vic20HalfCycleComparatorTests fixture, which requires absent HalfCycleState/CompareHalfCycleStates and is outside the authorized 20-name failure set. No managed/native tests or native builds run.

Revision 3 is not execution-ready on current evidence. Static source inspection shows Slice 1 reset-time regeneration does not preserve the required xvic PAL and NTSC 100000-cycle checkpoints and module-name coverage does not preserve the full manifest field contract. The full Nuke Test filter also selects the uncategorized managed-only Vic20HalfCycleComparator reflection test; its HalfCycleState and CompareHalfCycleStates targets do not exist, outside the R9 twenty-name CPU baseline. These are plan and dependency findings, not test execution results. The R11 cross-object wrap is feasible for fresh MAINCPU registers on both machines; architectural P must use the pinned accessor, and the CPU module return is not whole-snapshot success. Supported client.SessionLog.QueryAsync returns this reviewer complete turn and processing dialog, establishing a viable primary full-content readback route. No native code or tests were built or run.

# Hostile validation round 3 (relaunch 3b, sandbox network access enabled): PLAN-NATIVERESTORE-001 revision 3 (Phase D plan) before execution

You are the independent hostile reviewer for this round: GPT-6.1-Sol at reasoning effort max through the Codex CLI on LAB-OMARCHY, workspace /home/sharpninja/github/vice-sharp, branch develop (the commit is recorded in request.jsonl and input-pins.json). The implementer is a Claude session (claude-fable-5-1-high@ClaudeCode); you are a different agent family by the operator's rule. This is round 3 of a plan review before any of its steps execute; nothing under native/vice has changed, and nothing may change during your review.

Round 1 (receipt docs/receipts/hv/20261020T122200-plan-nativerestore-001-gpt61sol/) returned DISAGREE 85/70; round 2 (receipt docs/receipts/hv/20261020T131300-plan-nativerestore-001-r2-gpt61sol/, verdict.json and verdict.md pinned here) returned DISAGREE 92/84 with F03, F04, F05, F10, N01 and R02 failing, U01 and U02 unknown, N02 and A04 to A06 as added ACs, and 18 PASS. The implementer verified every round 2 finding against source and rewrote the plan as revision 3; section 7 of the plan maps each finding of both rounds to its amendment. Your job is to re-verify against the live sources, not to re-read your own round 2 as truth: for every round 2 finding state PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN with evidence (one entry per round 2 id), then attack the whole revised plan again for anything new that the amendments introduced, in particular the R10 launch precondition, the R11 B snapshot observer design, the Slice 1 obligation map and the N02 resume-boundary rules.

CREDENTIAL RULE (round 1 R01 was yours): do NOT read, cat, print, copy or quote AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml or any file holding an API key, in any shell, helper or tool call. The supported plugin reads the marker itself; you only call its wrappers through file-based PowerShell helpers, never inline PowerShell that echoes file contents. If any output you produce would contain a credential, stop that command. This is a hard rule of the operator and of this request.

TIMESTAMP RULE (round 2 R02 was yours): every progress object and every timestamp you emit is measured at the moment of emission by a command, never estimated or backfilled.

FIRST: run the add-profile skill exactly as its SKILL.md says (read every non-skill *.md under /home/sharpninja/.claude/profile in full; currently PROFILE-MERGED.md). Bootstrap your own supported plugin (mcpserver-codex-plugin, root /home/sharpninja/github/mcpserver-codex-plugin; verify with Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status) and open your own review session-log turn through it, titled with a short summary of this request, linked to the parent ids in this directory's request.jsonl (parentSessionId, parentRequestId). Rounds 1 and 2 reported the Codex plugin untrusted (MCP_UNTRUSTED, health nonce permission denied). Cause found 14:13: the Codex workspace-write sandbox denied outbound network, so the plugin's HTTP health check to the McpServer failed; this launch passes sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true, and the plugin reports available from an unsandboxed shell on this host. If the plugin still reports untrusted, record the exact error and the sandbox arguments from request.jsonl. If trust is still broken here: report the exact error, do not repair hooks, settings or environment, do not replay queues, do not cancel historical turns, attempt the supported triage once, then use the authorized full-content failsafe and label queued versus persisted. Do not invoke nested reviewers, do not substitute the model. There are no time or turn bounds on this review.

MANDATORY live progress: before analysis and at meaningful checkpoints, emit a TEXT JSON object into your output with timestampLocal (measured), numeric completionPercent and etaSeconds (null only if genuinely unknown). These are your own reports, not deadlines.

Operator rulings verbatim (treat as acceptance criteria): D4 (2026-10-19): native restoration approved; "Build artifacts are not code dirt. They should be gitignored."; "restore native/vice means revert the tracked modifications after preserving them, and exclude the build output through git ignore rules instead of deleting it". D3: "No HV until your current scope of work is complete and passes 98/98 holistic self-assessment", clarified "This is a remediation/cleanup phase, not new code"; on 2026-10-20T12:21 the operator stated that plans are hostile-validated under the standing rules, which is why these rounds exist. 10:40: "Wait for the Windows trace results first" (now satisfied: Windows 100k, 1M and x64sc 4M equal to Linux, receipt docs/receipts/lockstep/20261020T102600-phase-c-step3-s3-s4c-equivalence-windows/). 10:53: "Before beginning phase D implementation, ensure both omarchy and legion2 have latest desktop build installed via nuke." (done on both). 10:57: R1 "B: .gitmodules ignore = untracked only"; R2 and R3 "A: retire it now"; R4 "Yes, exclude and keep"; R5 "Yes, add in D2". 12:09: "Hold until LEGION2 reports". 13:03: R6 "A: ShimLegacy category (Recommended)"; R7 "A: reject all three (Recommended)"; R8 "A: observer -autostart .vsf (Recommended)"; R9 "A: known-red set of 20 (Recommended)". 14:06: R10 "A: adapter launch precondition (Recommended)"; R11 "B: require a native register observer" (chosen against the implementer's note that per-cycle registers are unreachable by wrapping; the plan implements it at the resume boundary through the global maincpu_regs written by maincpu_snapshot_read_module). Standing rules: never move a file (copy, verify by hash, retain the original until the operator clears deletion); never force-push; PowerShell only, no Python, no Node; every script analyzer-checked and dry-run with -WhatIf; BDPv4 mocks first for every behavior change; VICE is immutable (never edit, patch, generate into, clean or restore native/vice outside this plan's approved steps).

Read end to end, rehashing every pin in input-pins.json before you start and disclosing any drift: docs/plans/PLAN-NATIVERESTORE-001.md (the subject, revision 3), the round 2 verdict.json and verdict.md, docs/receipts/handoff/HANDOFF.lockstep-plan.md section 4 Phase D (line 115 is the exit) and Phase F (line 130 onward), docs/receipts/handoff/HANDOFF.lockstep-plan.v2.md sections 4 and 11, docs/plans/PLAN-VICE-IMMUTABLE-001.md (Phase 0, Phase 3, Phase 4 field set), docs/receipts/native-vice/20261004T090000-0500-preexisting-delta/README.md, its patch (all 20 hunks) and native-vice-untracked-paths.txt, docs/plans/PLAN-OBSERVER-001.md (S5), docs/plans/PLAN-VSFLOCKSTEP-001.md Slice 1 (lines 321 to 350), docs/requirements/technical/TR-Native-Vice-Snapshot.md (AC1 and AC2), docs/receipts/lockstep/20261019T202802-phase-e-step2-diagnostic-linux/README.md, tests/ViceSharp.TestHarness/ViceSharp.TestHarness.csproj, tests/ViceSharp.TestHarness/ViceFactAttribute.cs, tests/ViceSharp.TestHarness/XmlDocsConventionTests.cs, tests/ViceSharp.TestHarness/LockstepValidator.cs, src/ViceSharp.Core/ViceNative.cs, src/ViceSharp.ViceCompatibility/X64ScSnapshotCompatibility.cs, native/Vice.Native.proj, .gitmodules, native/build-vice-observer.ps1, tools/immutable-vice/Invoke-ObserverEquivalence.ps1, tools/immutable-vice/clock-observer-x64sc.c (the existing wrapper pattern), build/Build.cs, ViceSharp.slnx, this directory's SELF-REVIEW.md. Verify the plan's state claims yourself: git -C native/vice status --porcelain=v1 -uall, git -C native/vice diff --stat, git submodule status, the semantic native consumers under tests (ViceNative., ViceNativeXvic, ViceNativeBridge, IViceNative, XvicOraclePrerequisites; count files and note plain-Fact users), the callers of Vice.Native.proj, and in the pinned materialization under artifacts/immutable-vice/cc67418cba58e71d8e70fd353e9de47199ad2075/source/vice/src (read only): autostart.c snapshot path, monitor.c -moncommands handling (line 2237 onward) and mon_parse.y dump command, drive-snapshot.c writer (135 to 165) and reader (317 to 339, 368 to 419, 540 to 550), drive-resources.c default type, mainc64cpu.c maincpu_regs (line 513) and maincpu_snapshot_read_module (line 934 onward), mainviccpu.c line 756 onward, c64-snapshot.c line 121 and vic20-snapshot.c line 129 (cross-object calls), and the byte layout of tests/ViceSharp.TestHarness/Fixtures/Vsf/ready-c64sc-truedrive.vsf. Read-only on everything outside this receipt directory; you may run read-only git and grep commands and managed dotnet test commands on the three native-safe projects; never build the full solution, never build native code, never touch native/vice or artifacts/immutable-vice.

Mandatory attack surfaces (profile 7.2): (1) every claim in the plan (counts, the 20-hunk classification H1 to H12 against the patch, the pinned-source facts, the fixture facts, what Phase C proved, the exit gate as amended); (2) workspace rules (honesty, receipts, MCP-only storage, PowerShell only, no Python, never move a file, VICE immutable, no silent exclusion or AC reduction); (3) requirements: class 1; mapping to TR-VSFLOCKSTEP-RESUME-001 AC1 and AC2, TEST-VICE-001 AC1 and AC2, TR-CYCLE-001 AC4 (managed, left pending), PLAN-VICEORACLE-001 tasks 4 and 5; the Slice 1 amendment and the AC2 reference change must preserve semantics; (4) the plan holistically: definition of done, blockers, phase dependencies (D-pre, D0 to D5, Phase E and F hand-offs), rollback (A03), both machines, the R10 precondition (does -drive<n>type 0 really skip the uninitialized copy in the pinned reader, and does it change anything else the resumed workload observes?), the R11 B observer (is maincpu_regs complete and fresh right after the real read; is the wrap point cross-object on both machines; does the extra wrapper alter the no-snapshot equivalence?), the obligation map (is every Slice 1 and AC1 obligation owned, with an immutable command, a test and evidence, on both hosts?), the N02 boundary rules, A04, A05, A06. Run the what-if pass per criterion (a fixture with a missing DRIVE module; a unit configured as NONE by resource; the moncommands playback not firing at launch; make emitting no link line; a shim consumer reached only through a helper; the known-red set changing between D2 and D5; interruption mid-revert on Windows with autocrlf). Chain rules to find deadlocks. Where the plan does not state an observable outcome, propose a valid AC with the step that owns it; adding a valid AC is a finding of kind "add AC", not a FAIL by itself unless the gap makes a step unsafe.

Save verdict.md, verdict.json and verdict.persistence.json in THIS directory (docs/receipts/hv/20261020T141600-plan-nativerestore-001-r3b-gpt61sol/). Required JSON fields: OverallVerdict (AGREE or DISAGREE), accuracyPercent, completenessPercent, passCount, failCount, unknownCount, findings (id, status PASS or FAIL or UNKNOWN or ADD-AC, severity, file and line or section, evidence, rationale, correction; one entry per round 2 finding id stating its disposition in revision 3, plus new ids), reviewerAgent, reviewerModel, reviewerEffort, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId, requestPath, responsePath. Persist the COMPLETE prose and JSON verdict, every finding and both scores, in your own session-log turn (ordered small chunks if the wrapper's argument limits require it; read back, reassemble, compare hashes, disclose any CRLF/LF normalization), complete the turn and prove its completed state with a history query; write that proof into verdict.persistence.json. A full-content failsafe is authorized only after a genuine primary failure including a failed triage submission; label queued versus persisted. End with the whole verdict in your output stream. OverallVerdict is AGREE only if every applicable surface passes and both scores are at least 98; do not inflate scores; a sub-98 score is DISAGREE even with zero FAIL. No commit, no push, no edit outside this directory.
